messages:
incident-bot: [PAGER] High cross-region tail latency detected for requests routed EU->US. Severity: SEV2. Affected route policy: `geo-steer-v3`. Alerts: p99 latency > 1.2s for 7m; error rate spike to 3% for eu-west1 clients. Paging alex-oncall, carla-sre, ben-netops.

alex-oncall: seeing ~25% of traffic from eu-west1 suddenly routed to us-east1, p99 jumps. Noticed a config push around 01:40 UTC last night that touched `geo-steer-v3`.

ben-netops: checking route-maps now, this looks like a policy precedence bug where `pin-exceptions` lost higher priority. pulling policy history.

carla-sre: @alex-oncall please run the regional-affinity rollback from runbook while I open a ticket with infra team. Runbook ref: https://console.redwood/runbooks/regional-affinity (step 4 => rollback policy).

alex-oncall: running rollback now. Command: 
```
# rollback to previous policy
rdwctl steering apply --policy geo-steer-v3 --revision 2024-11-17-02
```

deploy-bot: deployment start: steering-policy geo-steer-v3 rev 2024-11-17-02 by alex-oncall. CID: dpl-7741.

carla-sre: (observing) policy reverted, but some clients still hit us-east due to DNS TTLs and cached pins. TTL currently 300s. Need to force drain or pin-expire.

ben-netops: we can expedite by temporarily creating a negative pin route for us-east1 so affinity will drop and traffic will re-evaluate. Preparing change: `steer add-exception --region us-east1 --expire-now`.

liam-sre: I'll take over on-call from alex in 10m. If we need provider-level assistance for BGP path flaps, escalate to netops@carrier.

maya-support: collecting customer impact details: support metrics show 12 high-priority customer sessions with >500ms degraded interactive latency in last 15m. No full service outage. Suggested customer comm: short advisory + ETA 2h.

sophie-product: Product wants an outbound note to trial customers. Keep it factual: degraded latency for EU requests routed to US for some endpoints; mitigation in progress.

ben-netops: applied negative-exception for us-east1, requesting immediate drain. Command: 
```
rdwctl steering add-exception --policy geo-steer-v3 --region us-east1 --action drain --force
```

deploy-bot: change complete: dpl-7742. Steering exception applied.

carla-sre: monitoring now. p50 fine, p95 dropping, p99 trending toward baseline. Error rate back to 0.5%. still seeing ~3% sticky sessions for some customers due to cached network pins (edge caches).

alex-oncall: note — the config diff shows the nighttime change toggled `prefer-latency=true` but also removed an explicit `region-affinity` rule. looks like an accidental overwrite during a canary. Raising a follow-up PR to prevent mutation of affinity rules.

liam-sre: taking ownership for the incident. I am oncall now and will drive next steps. Postmortem owner: carla-sre.

maya-support: current customer impact summary: ~18% of EU-origin requests experienced latency degradation at peak (p99 +400ms). ~0.8% requests returned 5xx correlated with cross-region timeouts. Affected endpoints: /v1/generate, /v1/chat. No billing anomalies reported.

carla-sre: immediate mitigation: rollback done, forced drain applied, TTL suggestion: lower to 60s for 10 minutes to accelerate healing. ben, can you coordinate a temporary TTL change at DNS edge?

ben-netops: submitted change to CDN DNS: set steer TTL=60 for geo-steer-v3 for 10m. Propagation estimate ~2m.

liam-sre: verifying customer-facing ETA. If all goes well, progressive recovery in 5-15 minutes, full stabilization in 1-2 hours as caches expire. Logging timeline and actions in the incident doc: https://incidents.redwood/1719994321.

alex-oncall: note for handoff: root cause suspected configuration mutation in canary pipeline that removed affinity rule. linked commits: https://git.redwood/steering/commit/abc123.

carla-sre: escalated to infra for a gating rule on steering configs. Action items: 1) postmortem (owner: carla-sre), 2) gating + schema validation on steering API (owner: dev-platform), 3) add monitoring alert for policy precedence changes (owner: observability).

maya-support: drafting customer advisory now. Will sync content with sophie-product. Will include mitigation steps and timeline.

sophie-product: please include apology, affected endpoints, and that no data loss occurred. Keep CTA to contact support for latency-sensitive tenants.

liam-sre: closing the active mitigation loop: p99 back to baseline for most routes, error rate normalized. I'll keep the thread open for postmortem and follow-ups. If anyone needs to join the postmortem, ping carla-sre. :thumbsup:
